newsitem.title: USA: HEI notified of phase-out of big contract.
newsitem.headline: HEI notified of phase-out of big contract.

text.p: HEI Inc said Monday it had received notice from its largest current customer to begin phasing out production of a microelectronic assembly used in high density disk drives.

The word of the phase-out was abrupt and counter to recent requests received from the customer for even higher volume shipments from HEI, along with compliments on HEI's performance, said Eugene Courtney, HEI chief executive officer, in a statement.
HEI said the customer, which was not named, indicated its intention to move ongoing production of this device off-shore, primarily to its own facility.
HEI said the phase out arrangements had not been finalized. It said it continues talks with the customer to reach a mutually satisfactory resolution in a timely fashion.

"Until these discussions reach a conclusion," said Courtney, "We will be unable to accurately assess the impact on our future revenues and earnings, but present indications are that significant effects of the phase out will commence in the fourth quarter of this fiscal year."

HEI will continue to pursue new opportunities in telecommunications and medical applications, as well as in the disk drive market, said Courtney. "We remain optimistic about our future growth prospects," he said.

HEI designs and makes ultraminiature microelectronic devices and high technology products incorporating those devices. The company had reported revenues of $20.7 million for its last fiscal year ended August 31, 1996.
Trading in shares of HEI was halted pending an announcement.
